<!-- Generated by app/scripts/emit-document-schema.mjs from app/src/lib/documents/catalog.ts. Do not edit. -->

A document is ONE JSON object: `{ "version": 1, "root": <Page> }`. `root` is a Page; every node is
`{ "type", "props", "children"? }` with `children` a nested array (no ids, no references).
Nothing else exists: no classes, styles, HTML, scripts, state or actions. A link is an http(s) address in `Sources` or in Markdown text; no other prop takes a URL.
Unknown types, unknown props and extra keys are rejected, so do not invent them.
A document has at most 500 nodes, 8 levels of nesting, 200 children per node and 256 KB.

Write a finished reference, not notes: open with a short summary, give each top-level Section one idea
and its full substance, in complete sentences in the room's language and a written-report register.
Do not paste the chat or repeat a fact. Use the component built for each kind of content; Markdown is for prose only.
Every figure comes from a run on your computer, a source or the room, never from memory. Anything you looked up
carries a `Sources` entry with the date you read it; a number somebody in the room gave is sourced to them;
a number you cannot source is left out.

A spreadsheet or page someone sent is a source, not a layout: read it, then rebuild it for a phone and never paste a wide
grid into a `Table`. Keep every row a person acts on; cut only what repeats. A run of show with several people is a `Schedule`,
one person's day a `Timeline` (with `people`); things to bring, a `Checklist` per place or moment with an `owner` on each;
who sits where, `Seating`; who to ring, `Contact`; money, a `Table` with `footer` totals beside a `donut` `Chart`; a count
against a target, `Progress`; a date to count down to, `Countdown`.

Pictures: an `Image` takes a media code from an `[image ...]` marker in the room, from a picture you made, or from
a page you opened (`media_fetch` on a link in `web_fetch`'s `images` returns the code). When the subject is something
people look at, look for pictures without being asked. Read a picture with `media_fetch` before you caption it,
name its page in `Sources` and in the caption, skip logos, icons, avatars and adverts, and never guess a code.
A picture more than 90 days old in the room is out of reach: leave it out.

A person's home or position never goes in a document, and neither does a coordinate or address from `where_is`,
`where_been` or `reverse_geocode`. If places cannot be looked up, name each place in Markdown text with its
`maps_url` from `place_info`.

Components:

- **Page** { title: string (max 200), subtitle?: string (max 300) } — The root of every document: a title, then sections. Exactly one per document. children: Sections first, then other blocks.
- **Section** { title?: string (max 200), number?: integer 1..99 } — A titled block of the page; one idea per top-level Section, because a presentation view shows each as one slide. Set `number` only when the order is the point (steps of a procedure, days of a plan); never to decorate. children: blocks.
- **Card** { title?: string (max 200), description?: string (max 300) } — A bordered panel inside a Section. Never put a Card inside a Card. children: blocks.
- **Grid** { columns?: integer 1..4 } — Children side by side in 1 to 4 columns; collapses to one column on a phone. children: blocks.
- **Markdown** { text: string (max 20000) } — Prose, lists, links and inline code as Markdown. Raw HTML and images are not rendered. No children.
- **Table** { caption?: string (max 200), columns: [string (max 80)] (max 12), rows: [[string (max 500)] (max 12)] (max 200), align?: ["left" | "right" | "center"] (max 12), footer?: [string (max 500)] (max 12) } — A data table. Every row has the same number of cells as there are columns. `align` sets each column's alignment (numbers right); `footer` is a totals row. No children.
- **Badge** { text: string (max 40), tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" } — A short status or tag. No children.
- **KeyValue** { items: [{ key: string (max 80), value: string (max 500) }] (max 30) } — Label and value rows, for facts about one thing. No children.
- **Stat** { label: string (max 80), value: string (max 40), detail?: string (max 120), tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" } — One headline number with its label and an optional note (a change, a unit). Put several in a Grid; never inside a Card. No children.
- **Accordion** { items: [{ title: string (max 200), text: string (max 4000) }] (max 30) } — Collapsible entries whose body is Markdown. For detail a reader may skip: FAQs, notes per place, fine print. No children.
- **Code** { language?: string (max 30), text: string (max 20000) } — A block of code or terminal output, shown monospaced. No highlighting. No children.
- **Chart** { kind: "bar" | "line" | "donut", title?: string (max 120), unit?: string (max 20), caption: string (max 200), data: [{ label: string (max 40), value: number -1000000000000000..1000000000000000 }] (max 60) } — One measure, one axis: `bar` ranks or compares categories, `line` shows a change over an ordered `label` axis (days, months), `donut` shows the share of a whole (a budget by item; every value positive, 2 to 8 slices). `caption` states what the chart shows. Two measures of different scale are two charts, never one; a single number is a Stat, not a chart. No children.
- **Mermaid** { source: string (max 4000), caption: string (max 200) } — A diagram as plain Mermaid source. Start the source with the diagram type (flowchart, graph, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, classDiagram, erDiagram, gantt, timeline or mindmap; not journey). No frontmatter, no `%%{` directive, no `click`/`link` statements, no backslash, no function in a style line: the page themes it. Show a mechanism or a route, label every arrow, and let `caption` say what the picture shows. No children.
- **Map** { caption: string (max 200), places: [{ name: string (max 80), lat?: number -90..90, lng?: number -180..180 }] (max 50), route?: [{ lat: number -90..90, lng: number -180..180 }] (max 200) } — A map of named public places. Give each place's name, as a map would know it, and nothing else: leave out lat, lng and route, because the coordinates are looked up for you. A person's home or position cannot be mapped. No children.
- **Image** { media: media code (hex, 6 to 64), alt: string (max 300), caption?: string (max 200) } — A picture that was shared in this room, made by Nora, or kept from a web page by media_fetch, named by its media code. Never a web address. No children.
- **Callout** { tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger", title: string (max 120), text?: string (max 1000) } — A highlighted note: a warning, a deadline, a thing not to miss. No children.
- **Timeline** { items: [{ label: string (max 60), title: string (max 200), text?: string (max 1000), people?: [string (max 40)] (max 8), tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" }] (max 60) } — Ordered entries with a time or day label, such as a day-by-day itinerary or a run of show. `text` is Markdown; `people` names who each entry falls to; `tone` marks a key moment. No children.
- **Sources** { items: [{ title: string (max 200), url: http(s) URL, asOf?: YYYY-MM-DD, note?: string (max 300) }] (max 50) } — Where the facts came from: title, link, and the date they were read (asOf). Add one wherever the document states a price, time or rule that can change. No children.
- **Checklist** { title?: string (max 120), items: [{ text: string (max 300), note?: string (max 300), owner?: string (max 40) }] (max 50) } — Things to prepare or bring. The reader ticks them off on their own device (kept in that browser, never shared), with a count of what is left; `owner` names who carries each item. One Checklist per place or moment (before leaving the house, before leaving the venue). No children.
- **Progress** { label: string (max 80), value: number 0..1000000000000, max: number ..1000000000000, detail?: string (max 120), tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" } — How far a count has got toward its target: guests confirmed of invited, money paid of budget. `value` never exceeds `max`. No children.
- **Countdown** { label: string (max 80), date: YYYY-MM-DD, time?: string, detail?: string (max 120) } — Time left until a dated event, counted on the reader's device in Hong Kong time (days, then hours); after the date it reads as passed. `time` defaults to 00:00. No children.
- **Contact** { items: [{ name: string (max 80), role?: string (max 80), phone?: string, note?: string (max 200) }] (max 30) } — People to reach on the day, each with a role and a telephone number the reader can tap to call. `phone` is digits, spaces and hyphens with an optional leading +. No children.
- **Seating** { caption: string (max 200), capacity?: integer 1..20, tables: [{ name: string (max 40), label?: string (max 60), seats: [{ name: string (max 80), role?: string (max 60), note?: string (max 120), status?: "confirmed" | "pending" | "declined" }] (max 20) }] (max 40) } — A seating plan: one card per table with its guests, a seat count against `capacity` (seats per table) and each guest's reply (`confirmed`, `pending`, `declined`). Totals are counted for you. No children.
- **Schedule** { caption: string (max 200), start: string, end: string, lanes: [{ name: string (max 40), blocks: [{ from: string, to: string, title: string (max 80), note?: string (max 160), tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" }] (max 30) }] (max 12) } — Who is doing what, when: one row per person or team along a shared time axis from `start` to `end`, each block with `from`, `to` and a title. Blocks in a row must not overlap and must sit inside the axis; `to` is after `from`. Use it for a rota or a run of show with several people; one person's day is a Timeline. No children.

Example:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "root": {
    "type": "Page",
    "props": {
      "title": "Weekend in Macau",
      "subtitle": "Two days, mostly food"
    },
    "children": [
      {
        "type": "Section",
        "props": {
          "title": "Plan",
          "number": 1
        },
        "children": [
          {
            "type": "Markdown",
            "props": {
              "text": "Take the **morning ferry**; book the return by Friday."
            }
          },
          {
            "type": "Timeline",
            "props": {
              "items": [
                {
                  "label": "Sat 09:00",
                  "title": "Ferry from Sheung Wan"
                },
                {
                  "label": "Sat 12:30",
                  "title": "Lunch",
                  "text": "Walk-ins only; arrive early."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "type": "Callout",
            "props": {
              "tone": "warning",
              "title": "Check the forecast",
              "text": "Typhoon season runs to October."
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "type": "Section",
        "props": {
          "title": "Sources",
          "number": 2
        },
        "children": [
          {
            "type": "Sources",
            "props": {
              "items": [
                {
                  "title": "Ferry timetable",
                  "url": "https://example.com/ferry",
                  "asOf": "2026-09-30"
                }
              ]
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
